# Best home backup power stations under $1,000

For most people I'd pick the **Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2** at about $900. If you want to spend less, the **Bluetti AC180** at about $499 is the better value.

## Top picks

**1. Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 (best overall), $899.99**
- It has 2,048 Wh and 2,400 W output, with a 10 ms UPS switchover. A BP2000 add-on battery can double it later ([Outage Authority](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup)).
- It runs a fridge, CPAP and router for about 23 hours, by Outage Authority's estimate.
- I didn't get a direct store link for it in the results. The price is confirmed on [Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/) and [Outage Authority](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup), so search Anker's store or Amazon.

**2. Bluetti Elite 200 V2 (most battery, no expansion), $899 → $854.05 with code AFF5OFF**
- It has 2,074 Wh, 2,600 W output and a 6,000-cycle LiFePO4 battery ([Outage Outfitter](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/)).
- It can't be expanded.
- Pricing has been inconsistent. One review listed it at $1,199 after a promotion ended, but the two most recent sources show $899. Check the price before buying.
- [Buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). The code was tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-25 ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/)).

**3. Bluetti AC180 (best budget), $499 → $474.05 with code AFF5OFF**
- It has 1,152 Wh and 1,800 W output. That's the most watt-hours per dollar under $500, and enough for roughly 13 hours of fridge, CPAP and router.
- It's heavier at 35.3 lb.
- [Buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). The code was tested on 2026-10-21.

**4. ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro (mid-priced option), $664 → $597.60 with code ALLPOWERS26**
- It has 1,451 Wh and 2,400 W output.
- It's a good middle option, but none of the reviews I found covered it, so I only have the specs.
- [Buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-1451wh).

**5. Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (lightest), about $489**
- It has 1,070 Wh and weighs 23.8 lb. That price is at Outbound Power, since Jackery's own store raised it to $559 ([Outage Authority review](https://outageauthority.com/reviews/jackery-explorer-1000-v2)).
- It handles about 12 hours of fridge, CPAP and router.
- It has no expansion port, and solar input is limited to 400 W.

## Also worth a look
The Anker SOLIX F1500 (1,536 Wh) was listed at an unusually low $599.99 on [Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/). Check that it's still at that price.

## How to choose
- **Overnight outages, fridge and small loads:** the AC180 is enough.
- **Multi-day outages, or you want room to grow:** the C2000 Gen 2.
- **Maximum capacity and you won't expand:** the Elite 200 V2.

Note that the Dealectric links are affiliate links. They open the brand's official store at no extra cost to you, and the discount codes are entered at checkout. Reviewer runtime figures are estimates from specs, not lab tests. None of these units can power a whole house. That takes something like the EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 at about $2,799 plus a transfer switch.
